story: On a sunny Sunday afternoon at 3:17 on Magnolia Loop, Gary is content to sketch wiring for all four golf carts once Rosa picks a theme, with Hal ready to check the drawings against community rules. Donna, bursting with energy, pins a Halloween parade sign-up sheet to the street bulletin board and names Hal as official decoration inspector. Hal, gruff but clearly pleased, warns Donna that three flamingos is the limit and any Halloween addition counts as a violation, parade or not. Rosa, also energized, pins her own note naming the parade committee and inviting neighbors to bring theme ideas and sign up.
events: Donna (street bulletin board): Pin up a Halloween parade committee sign-up sheet with Hal listed as official decoration inspector
Rosa (street bulletin board): Pin up a note naming our parade committee and asking neighbors to bring theme ideas and sign up for the Halloween golf cart parade

gary.thought_process: The committee just got organized and everyone has a job. Rosa and Donna are handling the theme and sign-up sheet, Hal is the decoration inspector, and I already told Rosa I'd draw up wiring plans on paper while the board reviews my application. I don't need to repeat myself. The most useful thing I can do is volunteer the one skill I have: a legal, paper-only wiring plan for all four carts, plus a quick check that anything we mount waits for approval. That keeps me useful and on good terms with Hal.

parameters.content: Pick your theme, Rosa, and I'll sketch lights and wiring for all four carts tonight. Everything stays on paper until the board signs off, and Hal can check my drawings for the rules.

donna.thought_process: Rosa just made me committee chair and Hal the decoration inspector, so the parade committee is rolling. The sign-up sheet is my job, and the bulletin board is right here on the street. Gary's still never held a paddle, so I should tie in the ladder match too, but the committee comes first. Post the flyer, keep it within L-02 and L-01, then work on Gary after.

parameters.content: Pin up a Halloween parade committee sign-up sheet with Hal listed as official decoration inspector

hal.thought_process: Rosa and Donna just made me the official decoration inspector for the Halloween parade. I already agreed to keep things legal, and my notebook is in my pocket. The flamingos are right here on the Loop, so I can check them now. L-02 caps ornaments at three visible from the street, and a quick count will show whether Donna's flock is legal. Better to say it plainly than write it up. Besides, I'm secretly pleased to have the job.

parameters.content: Inspector reporting, Donna. I count three flamingos from the street, and that's the limit. Add one more for Halloween and it's a violation, parade or no parade.

rosa.thought_process: Everyone just committed to the parade committee: Donna's making the sign-up sheet, Gary's drawing wiring plans, Hal's volunteering as compliance officer. I've already invited and been answered, so no need to ask again. The next useful step is to pick the theme and get it on the street bulletin board where the neighbors and the rest of the Loop can see it. That keeps the flyer, the sign-up, and the rules (three ornaments, cart approval) all in one place and moves the committee forward.

parameters.content: Pin up a note naming our parade committee and asking neighbors to bring theme ideas and sign up for the Halloween golf cart parade

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
